strengths: Tackles an important and timely challenge in 3D computer vision: developing an open-world, promptable 3D foundation model for part segmentation that works natively in 3D rather than relying solely on multi-view 2D lifting.

Well-motivated architecture: The dual-branch encoder effectively balances retaining 2D foundation priors (via a frozen branch initialized with PartField) while adapting to native 3D geometric supervision and auxiliary modalities (via the learnable branch with zero-convolutions).

Effective model-in-the-loop data curation: The proposed strategy combines geometric scene graphs/connected components with an interactive verification loop (using PartField proposals filtered via simulated multi-turn interaction) to scale 3D part supervision to over 5 million parts.

Strong empirical performance: PartSAM achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art methods in both interactive segmentation (e.g., +91% relative improvement at IoU@1 over Point-SAM) and automatic class-agnostic decomposition on PartObjaverse-Tiny and PartNetE.

Insightful analysis of evaluation pitfalls: Section A.2.4 provides a valuable analysis demonstrating that mesh connectivity in artist-created datasets acts as an unfair shortcut/label leak, motivating a fairer benchmark protocol without mesh connectivity.
weaknesses: Evaluation is confined to clean synthetic/generated 3D assets: The benchmarks (PartObjaverse-Tiny, PartNet-E) and qualitative examples (Hunyuan3D) consist almost entirely of synthetic CAD or artist/AI-generated meshes. Performance on noisy, incomplete real-world 3D scans (e.g., RGB-D object reconstructions or physical LiDAR/sensor data) is not explored.

Heavy reliance on PartField across the pipeline: Both branches of the encoder are initialized from PartField, one branch remains frozen with PartField representations, and the model-in-the-loop data generation heavily depends on PartField cluster proposals. While pragmatic and effective, the framework is strongly coupled with the pre-existence of PartField.

Analysis of hyperparameters for 'Segment Every Part' is limited: The automatic mode relies on several heuristic choices (number of FPS prompt points $N_f$, IoU confidence thresholds, and NMS threshold $T$). A sensitivity analysis showing how varying $N_f$ and $T$ influences runtime and segmentation granularity would provide greater practical guidance.

strengths: PartSAM presents a well-motivated and principled adaptation of the SAM paradigm to native 3D data, moving beyond the surface-level limitations of 2D mask lifting and feature clustering methods.

The dual-branch encoder architecture is cleverly designed to balance large-scale native 3D learning with preserved 2D foundational priors (distilled from SAM via PartField), effectively preventing catastrophic forgetting while incorporating additional surface attributes.

The model-in-the-loop data curation pipeline is practical and scalable, creatively combining connected-component heuristics with iterative interactive filtering to curate over 5 million high-quality 3D part annotations.

Empirical performance is substantially superior to prior work, exhibiting a dramatic gain over Point-SAM in interactive segmentation (e.g., IoU@1 increasing from 29.4% to 56.1% on PartObjaverse-Tiny) and state-of-the-art automatic segmentation results.

The analysis of mesh connectivity bias/leakage on artist-created meshes versus AI-generated meshes provides important insights and sets a rigorous evaluation standard for future 3D part segmentation research.
weaknesses: The thresholds chosen for the model-in-the-loop filtering (e.g., IoU@1 > 60 or IoU@10 > 90) appear empirical; a brief sensitivity analysis on these filtering thresholds would strengthen the dataset construction section.

While Table 5 reports total shape segmentation time (~12s for Segment Every Part), it does not explicitly quantify single-prompt interactive latency (per-click latency), which is crucial for evaluating interactive user workflows.
The method remains class-agnostic without semantic label output, requiring external models or text grounding for semantic categorization (though this is reasonably acknowledged as future work).
Minor typographic errors are present in the text (e.g., 'duan-branch transformer' on page 2).

strengths: A well-motivated and comprehensive framework that brings the promptable segmentation paradigm (akin to 2D SAM) directly to native 3D geometry, overcoming key limitations of 2D lifting methods (surface-only understanding, lack of internal structures, expensive per-shape optimization) and feature clustering methods (lack of interactive controllability, reliance on mesh connectivity).

The dual-branch triplane encoder is thoughtfully designed: freezing one branch initialized with PartField retains 2D foundation priors distilled from SAM, while the learnable branch absorbs native 3D supervision and auxiliary attributes (normals, RGB) without catastrophic forgetting, as validated in the ablation studies.

The two-stage data curation and model-in-the-loop annotation pipeline is effective and scalable, producing over 5 million shape-part pairs from 500k 3D assets to enable robust open-world generalization.

Substantial empirical gains: PartSAM outperforms Point-SAM by 91% relative IoU with a single prompt point on interactive segmentation, and exceeds state-of-the-art automatic segmentation methods (PartField, SAMPart3D, SAMesh) by over 10-13% absolute IoU on PartObjaverse-Tiny and PartNetE.

Insightful analysis regarding evaluation pitfalls in the literature; specifically, the paper exposes how mesh connectivity in artist-created datasets like PartObjaverse-Tiny can leak ground-truth part boundaries to clustering-based baselines.
weaknesses: The model is strictly class-agnostic and does not predict semantic part labels or text-aligned categories, leaving open-vocabulary semantic part identification to downstream pipelines or future extensions.

Prompt modalities are currently restricted to positive/negative 3D click points and previous mask logits; support for 3D bounding boxes, bounding spheres, or text prompts is not integrated into the prompt encoder.

The 'Segment Every Part' automatic decomposition relies on sampling fixed numbers of FPS points followed by point-level NMS, which introduces heuristic hyperparameters (such as NMS threshold T and point sample count Nf) that affect the granularity of segmentation across diverse shape scales.

Potential risk of pseudo-label noise: While the model-in-the-loop filtering criteria (IoU@1 > 60 or IoU@10 > 90) eliminate many fragmented components, errors inherited from PartField clustering could still propagate into the pseudo-labeled training corpus.

strengths: Addresses a fundamental limitation of existing 2D-lifting part segmentation methods: their inability to perceive interior 3D structures and handle non-manifold/unconnected AI-generated geometry.

Well-motivated dual-branch encoder architecture that effectively bridges pre-trained 2D SAM priors (via a frozen contrastively-trained branch) with scalable native 3D representation learning (via a learnable branch accommodating coordinates, normals, and colors).

Novel and scalable model-in-the-loop data curation pipeline that leverages connected components, scene graphs, and iterative interactive filtering to construct a diverse native 3D dataset containing over 5 million shape-part pairs.

Outstanding empirical results across interactive and automatic segmentation benchmarks, achieving substantial improvements over existing state-of-the-art approaches like Point-SAM (e.g., +91% relative IoU at 1 prompt) and PartField.

Comprehensive experimental analysis, including thorough ablation studies, scaling curves, complexity/runtime comparisons, downstream applications (interior part editing, amodal completion), and honest analysis of failure cases.
weaknesses: The data generation and model initialization rely heavily on pre-existing models (specifically PartField for initialization and candidate generation), creating an algorithmic and data dependency on prior contrastive 2D-to-3D distillation.

The model is restricted to class-agnostic part masks and lacks semantic text/label grounding, which limits immediate applicability to open-vocabulary semantic part retrieval without an additional vision-language module.

The multi-stage data curation heuristic (filtering by connected components count and PartSAM IoU thresholds) might introduce bias against very fine-grained parts (e.g., small embossed details, engravings), as observed in the failure cases.

strengths: Compelling and timely conceptual motivation: adapting the promptable, foundational segmentation paradigm of SAM natively to 3D geometry rather than relying on noisy 2D multi-view mask lifting or post-hoc heuristic feature clustering.

Well-engineered architecture: the dual-branch triplane encoder elegantly addresses the stability/generalization trade-off by keeping a frozen branch initialized with 2D SAM-distilled priors while training a learnable branch on native 3D shapes with auxiliary geometric attributes.

Practical and effective data curation strategy: the model-in-the-loop annotation pipeline leverages simulated interactive refinement to filter out noisy component clustering, successfully scaling training data to over 5 million native 3D shape-part pairs.

Strong and thorough empirical validation: PartSAM demonstrates substantial performance gains over existing methods (e.g., Point-SAM, SAMPart3D, SAMesh, PartField) on both interactive and automatic segmentation benchmarks, exhibiting superior ability to segment internal/occluded parts and AI-generated non-watertight meshes.
Comprehensive supplementary material, providing extensive ablation studies, scaling analysis up to 500k shapes, inference efficiency comparisons, and candid failure analysis.
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on PartField: the framework depends significantly on PartField both for initializing the encoder weights (to retain SAM priors) and for generating candidate pseudo-labels in the data curation stage, making the training pipeline complex and multi-stage.

Lack of semantic/text prompt conditioning: the model is purely geometry/point-prompt-based and class-agnostic; unlike multimodal foundation models, it cannot directly associate discovered parts with text semantics or open-vocabulary linguistic queries.

Part granularity ambiguity in automatic segmentation: while the NMS threshold allows coarse-to-fine adjustments, selecting the ideal granularity for unseen shapes without semantic context remains heuristic, occasionally leading to over- or under-segmentation.

strengths: Compelling and impactful contribution: PartSAM addresses major bottlenecks in 3D part segmentation (such as surface-only understanding in 2D lifting methods and lack of controllability in 3D clustering methods) by presenting a native 3D promptable encoder-decoder framework.

Well-motivated architecture: The dual-branch encoder structure successfully mitigates catastrophic forgetting of 2D foundation priors (from distilled SAM) while enabling native 3D representation learning and incorporation of additional modalities like surface normals and RGB.

Effective large-scale data curation: The two-stage automated curation pipeline—integrating scene graphs/connected components and using a model-in-the-loop verification mechanism with PartField—scales native 3D shape-part annotations to over 5 million pairs, supported by convincing scaling analysis.

Superior empirical performance: Outperforms existing baselines by decisive margins across multiple benchmarks (e.g., over +20% absolute IoU gain in automatic segmentation on PartObjaverse-Tiny and PartNetE, and massive improvements in interactive single-click segmentation).

Capability on occluded and interior geometry: Demonstrates convincing qualitative and quantitative advantages in segmenting interior and non-visible structures, where multi-view 2D lifting approaches inherently fail.
weaknesses: Heavy architectural and data dependency on PartField: Both encoder initialization and the candidate pseudo-label generation for stage-2 data curation depend directly on PartField, which limits the method from being fully self-contained.

Heuristic thresholds in data curation: The filtering criteria for the model-in-the-loop pipeline (e.g., IoU@1 > 60 or IoU@10 > 90, shape-level threshold of >5 parts) are somewhat arbitrary, and sensitivity analyses regarding these thresholds are missing.
Lack of semantic category prediction: As with 2D SAM, the model is strictly class-agnostic and produces masks without semantic labels, requiring separate mechanisms for semantic part parsing.

Struggles with thin surface details and open-world ambiguities: As highlighted in the failure cases, fine-grained surface markings (such as engraved text) and shapes lacking clear topological part hierarchies remain challenging.
